skill.name: ddd-context-mapping
skill.description: Map relationships between bounded contexts and define integration contracts with DDD context mapping patterns.
skill.summary: Map bounded context relationships, ownership, translation rules, and integration risks.
skill.author: sickn33

security_audit.summary: The two static findings are false positives caused by Markdown inline code and a fenced text example. I found no prompt injection, data exfiltration intent, executable scripts, or malicious semantic behavior in the reviewed skill files.

static_findings.snippet: If detailed mapping structures are needed, open `references/context-map-patterns.md`.

finding_verdicts.reason: Line 31 uses Markdown inline code to name references/context-map-patterns.md. It instructs the model to open a local reference file and does not execute a shell command.
Lines 42-45 are a fenced text example showing how to invoke the skill. The backticks are Markdown formatting, not Ruby or shell execution.

content.value_statement: Teams often miss ownership, translation, and coupling risks between bounded contexts. This skill guides context mapping, contract ownership, anti-corruption decisions, and integration risk planning.
actual_capabilities: Lists bounded context pairs and dependency direction.
Selects DDD relationship patterns for each integration.
Defines contract ownership and translation boundaries.
Identifies coupling risks, failure modes, and mitigation plans.
Uses a reference template for mapping structures.
limitations: It does not replace API-level schema design.
It cannot resolve team ownership conflicts by itself.
It needs accurate context and dependency information.
It does not generate executable integration code.

use_cases.title: Plan service boundaries
use_cases.description: Map how services depend on each other before committing to integration patterns.

use_cases.title: Protect domain language
use_cases.description: Define translation rules that keep external models out of a core domain.

use_cases.title: Prepare migration integrations
use_cases.description: Plan anti-corruption layers and fallback behavior during legacy system replacement.

prompt_templates.title: Map basic dependencies
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner context mapping for known services.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use ddd-context-mapping to map Checkout, Billing, Inventory, and Fraud. Show dependency direction and likely relationship patterns.

prompt_templates.title: Choose integration patterns
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate pattern selection for multiple bounded contexts.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use ddd-context-mapping to compare Partnership, Customer-Supplier, Conformist, and Anti-Corruption Layer options for these context pairs.

prompt_templates.title: Plan an anti-corruption layer
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced migration planning across old and new domains.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use ddd-context-mapping to design an anti-corruption layer between Legacy Orders and Fulfillment. Include translation rules and failure behavior.

prompt_templates.title: Review context map governance
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced review for ownership, versioning, and risk.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use ddd-context-mapping to audit this context map for contract ownership, versioning policy, coupling risks, and mitigation actions.

output_examples.input: Checkout integrates with Billing, Inventory, and Fraud.
output: Checkout is downstream of Billing for payment status and contract changes.
Inventory should expose a published language for stock reservations.
Fraud may need an anti-corruption layer if its risk terms differ from Checkout.

output_examples.input: A team is replacing legacy Orders with new Fulfillment.
output_examples.output: The skill would recommend a migration map with Legacy Orders upstream at first, Fulfillment protected by translation rules, and explicit fallback behavior.

output_examples.input: Identity owns user attributes used by Checkout.
output_examples.output: The skill would likely classify Checkout as conforming to Identity unless Checkout needs its own domain language or validation rules.

best_practices: Start with known context pairs and actual dependency direction.
Name the contract owner for every integration.
Review the map when team ownership or domain language changes.
anti_patterns: Do not use context mapping as a substitute for API contract design.
Do not assume every integration needs an anti-corruption layer.
Do not ignore failure modes and versioning policy.

faq.question: What does this skill help produce?
faq.answer: It helps produce a context relationship map, contract ownership matrix, translation decisions, and coupling risk plan.

faq.question: Does it design API schemas?
faq.answer: No. It helps decide ownership and integration patterns before detailed API schema work.

faq.question: Can it help with legacy migration?
faq.answer: Yes. It can plan anti-corruption layers, translation rules, fallback behavior, and temporary dependency direction.

faq.question: Which DDD patterns does it cover?
faq.answer: It covers Partnership, Shared Kernel, Customer-Supplier, Conformist, Anti-Corruption Layer, Open Host Service, and Published Language.

faq.question: What information should I provide?
faq.answer: Provide bounded contexts, dependency direction, data exchanged, owning teams, and known domain language conflicts.

faq.question: Does it work in Claude, Codex, and Claude Code?
faq.answer: Yes. The report lists compatibility with Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.
